consensus_summary: Understanding is primarily God-given spiritual discernment: the capacity to perceive, grasp, and rightly apply divine truth, moral order, and God's will, closely paired with wisdom and rooted in the fear of the Lord (often as illumination or Spirit gift rather than mere natural intellect).
book_summary: Understanding is discernment of good from evil, gained by departing from evil; those who do God's commandments have good understanding.
consensus_core_identification: God-given spiritual/moral discernment of divine truth and will
book_core_identification: Discernment of good from evil obtained by departing from evil
boundary_disagreement: Book conditions and restricts understanding definitionally to moral discernment of good/evil acquired specifically via departing from evil or commandment-keeping; consensus admits broader cases of Spirit-enabled insight into Scripture, mysteries, wisdom literature, technical skill, or formal gifts of the Spirit not so conditioned.
material_contradiction: None; the book's identification is already present inside the consensus primary (e.g., Job 28:28 and discernment of good and evil) and moral-discernment alternatives.
rationale: Minimum cores share the same general category of (moral/spiritual) discernment. The book preserves that referent but materially narrows extension, boundary, and conditions by elevating the Job 28:28 / Ps 111:10 equation into the definition itself and excluding the wider range of God-given insight, scriptural illumination, and Spirit endowments that consensus primaries treat as central. This is boundary refinement, not core replacement or novelty.
strongest_objection: Consensus primarily frames understanding as a prior divine gift enabling discernment and obedience, so treating it as the result gained by departing from evil may invert or over-restrict the causal and semantic range found across the broader biblical data.
